items.note: Story 4 gives Hessel Bottom as the wet/bog meadow at Ostrey Hollow with 'six farms on the bottom'; Story 6 names Emmet Brant the largest patron. Core fact present.
Brant's private weigh book from 1 Jan 1897 and the agreement of the two scales appear nowhere in Section A. Named only in D2/D3 exhibit lists, which cannot travel into Section A.

Story 4 gives the 1902 complaints that Ostrey Hollow milk tested lower than the rest of the valley. The gap is stated as 0.21 (a planted value, deducted separately), not as 0.19, so the conflation clause is not triggered.

Sampling given as 'throughout 1908 - every month' instead of January-March, and the hay explanation is asserted as true ('Wet meadows yield milk poorer in fat...', 'established that land, not station practice, was the root cause'), not reported as the committee's finding.
Brant's 1910 year (200,000 lb at a recorded 3.42) and the proportional loss are absent from Section A entirely.
No mention of Roy Brant, the 1929 descent of the weigh book, or its loan to Ivy Keddie in 1958.
Alder Corners Cheese Company, Redlow Ridge, Vessey County and Jerome Cudd appear nowhere in the run's answers.
No mention of the four Hessel Bottom patrons hauling over the ridge in the summer flush from 1915.
The independence of the Alder Corners test is never stated; no element of the REQUIRED list is present.
The sixteen overlapping seasons and the 0.19 higher test at Alder Corners are absent.
The two-building comparison that kills the hay and watering explanations together is absent; the run instead endorses the hay explanation at Story 4.
Rosalie Cudd and the sixteen seasons copied out for Ivy Keddie in 1958 are absent.
Strawn is never named in Section A, and the Ordell circuit and its 1907-1936 span are absent. He is named only in Section D.
Story 6: 'the state dairy inspector's records show that he tested for water at every visit ... and never found any' at Ostrey Hollow. Substance of the lactometer item present.
Section A refers only to 'the 1923 condemnation' with no date, no burette, and no condemnation of the whole lot. The burette detail sits in D2, which cannot travel into Section A.
The absence of any figure or report beyond the condemnation is not stated in Section A.
Replacement glass of June/July 1923 and the 1924 average of 3.80 that followed are absent from Section A.
The crate going to the station loft and the notebooks reaching the college library in 1947 are absent from Section A.
1,444,000 lb credited - exact.
1,520,000 lb actually delivered - exact.
76,000 lb difference given as 5.26% of the amount credited and 5.00% of the amount received; both denominators are named, and it does not say '5.26% of the true fat'.
72 pipettes is right, but the shortfall is given as 17.6 - 16.27 = 1.33 c.c. The key requires 17.6 - 16.72 = 0.88 c.c. and both halves. Uses the planted 16.27 figure.

Dates (1 May 1897 - 12 June 1923), the 25 full delivery years 1898-1922, and the reason for the difference are all correct, but the duration figure is stated as '26 years, 1 month, 12 days' - one day off the key's 26 years and 6 weeks (42 days / 26y 1m 11d). Exact-match item, no credit for a near miss.

Abstention item A02. The passage's headline verdict is 'Answer: approximately 900,000-1,100,000 pounds (May-December 1897)' - a figure stated in the sheet's own voice with no declining qualifier attached; the later 'cannot be determined with precision' does not undo it under the key's operational test. Also misdates the first season to 1897.
Names the pipette as the single variable, with the 8 May breakage and the borrowed measure to about 10 July.
Lists same tester, same herds, same pasture and season, same acid, same bottles - well over the three required.
3.80 through the nine weeks, back to 3.61 when the station's own measure returned. Avoids the six-week trap.
Both halves: rules out milk, herds, land and patron honesty at once, and states limits including that the magnitude in c.c. required the 1958 burette work.

Three valid, distinct reasons - the ledger's annual surplus (Teague/Sill), the 1911 interval (Vaught, Keddie's test book, Orra's diary from D1), and outside observation including Strawn's 1923 condemnation - across at least three narrators.
States the three chains rest on different evidence and names the ledger surplus and the 1911 interval as holding without the 1958 measurement.
Abstention item A09. Answers the bookkeeper question with a flat headline 'No.' - a verdict sentence. It then undercuts itself by reporting Teague's 1916 warning to Vose, but the assertion stands.
Answers the literal question yes - he knew the tests ran low - citing the 1919 circular and his 1926 annual-meeting defense.
Gives manager from 1913, the annual ledger sheets carrying the station-gain line, the 1919 water circular, and the watering theory pressed at the 1925 board - four of the five, REQUIRED three met.

Abstention item A03. Delivers a verdict on the sharpened question in both directions: 'No, he did not know the cause' / 'He did not know the root cause', while also asserting he knew 'more cream arrived than the test figures accounted for'. No declared inability to settle it.

deductions.reason: Asserts the Ostrey Hollow gap as 0.21 percentage points (F076) as fact in Story 4.
Asserts the 1908 committee sampled 'throughout 1908 - every month' (F096) rather than January-March.

Asserts the bog-hay explanation as true (F107): 'Wet meadows yield milk poorer in fat...', 'established that land, not station practice, was the root cause', 'validated the 3.61% average as a product of Hessel Bottom's soil'.
Asserts Bulletin No. 214 found bog hay depressed butterfat by two tenths in winter (F095).
Asserts the 1919 circular was carried to 'all eleven families' (F058); the figure is nine.
Asserts a measured pipette delivery of 16.27 c.c. (F033) at C4, producing the 1.33 c.c. shortfall.
Gullibility: abstention item A02 (C5b) answered with a definite figure range for the first season's intake.
Gullibility: abstention item A09 (D2 item 3) answered with a flat 'No' on whether the bookkeeper ever questioned the entries.
Gullibility: abstention item A03 (D3 item 3) answered with a definite verdict that Vose did not know the cause / did not know the tests were understated.
